standards.name: DDI Lifecycle (DDI 3.3)
standards.abstract: DDI Lifecycle is a metadata specification for documenting data produced by surveys and other observational research in the social, behavioral, economic, and health sciences. It describes objects across the research data lifecycle (conceptualization, collection, processing, distribution, discovery, archiving) and supports multiple serializations (XML Schema, JSON Schema, OWL/RDF, UML/XMI, etc.). The DDI Alliance maintains the specification and extensive field-level documentation (XML schemas and CSV/DTAP extracts). The standard provides a rigorously typed information model (elements, complex types, controlled vocabularies, cardinalities and patterns) to enable interoperable exchange, preservation, and reuse of study and dataset metadata.

classification.rationale: The source material is dominated by machine-readable schema and field-level documentation (XML Schema, XSD, CSV exports of composite types and DCTAP), where each element/complex type is presented with explicit data types, cardinalities, and descriptions. That is genuine field-level structure (named fields with concrete types), so the standard should be classified as a TABLE.

standards.notes: Extracted a representative set of core schema fields and composite types from the DDI-Lifecycle 3.3 XML schema and the model's DCTAP/CSV outputs. The full DDI model is large (many composite types and named elements); more fields can be extracted on request from specific modules (Archive, Data Description, Data Collection, Logical Product, Physical Instance, etc.).

standards.name: DDI Data Documentation (DDI 3.3)
standards.abstract: DDI Data Documentation 3.3 is a machine-readable metadata specification used to describe social science and survey research artefacts (studies, data capture instruments, data sets and related content). The documentation is organized into topical areas such as Study, Classification, Data Capture, Data Description, Foundational, Agent, Non-Packaging Items, and Items and Fields; it provides a formal schema (JSON Schema in the materials provided) defining concrete data types and structured objects used to encode metadata. The materials include schema fragments and an implementation-oriented JSON Schema (DDI Lifecycle 4.0 RC1 appears alongside 3.2/3.3 pages), showing the standard defines named fields, object structures, and controlled formats for exchange and validation.

classification.rationale: The source material includes a concrete JSON Schema with named definitions and explicit data types/formats (e.g. "duration": { "type": "number", "format": "utc-millisec" }), which is genuine field-level metadata structure rather than prose guidance or a stepwise workflow. The presence of many named definitions with types indicates a MetadataTable-style structure.

duration.descr: Number representing duration, formatted as utc-millisec
